title: To be developed
hook: the fourth truth's task is to be walked (SN 56.11)

segments.voice: Yesterday: magga, the fourth truth, eight factors working like strands of a rope. Your line: the path.

Every town has a path across a field that no one planned. No sign, no pavement. People kept walking from the bus stop to the shop until the grass gave up and a line of bare earth appeared. Nobody built it in a day, and nobody owns it. It exists because it was walked. The first sermon gives the fourth truth a task that works the same way. Not to be admired, not to be memorized: to be developed, by walking it.
screen: `A PATH NO ONE PLANNED.` → `THE GRASS GAVE UP.` → `IT EXISTS BECAUSE IT WAS WALKED.`

segments.voice: The task is bhāvetabba: to be developed, cultivated, brought into being. It comes from the verb to be, or to become, the same family as bhāvanā, one of the most common Pali words for meditation. So meditation, in this language, isn't mainly sitting still. It's bringing something into being by doing it again and again, like that path across the field. Now hold all four tasks together. Dukkha is to be understood. Craving is to be let go. Its ending is to be realized. The path is to be developed. Four truths, four verbs, and the sermon never swaps them. One way to see why: try to let go of dukkha, and you'll fight your own life. Try to understand craving forever, and you'll keep feeding it while you study it. Try to develop the ending, and you'll strain after something that comes by letting go. Each truth gets the job that fits it. Here's the week, from the top. Samudaya, the second truth: three thirsts, for pleasure, for being, for not-being. To be let go: Ananda's walk to the park, a wish that ends on arrival. Nirodha, the third truth: the burden set down. Nibbana: the fire going out, Sariputta's one-sentence answer. To be realized: the ocean with one taste. Magga, the fourth truth: eight factors like strands of a rope. And today, to be developed, the one task you can start on any Tuesday, with a single step.
screen: `BHĀVETABBA: TO BE BROUGHT INTO BEING.` · `FOUR TRUTHS, FOUR VERBS.` · `EACH TRUTH GETS ITS JOB.` · `THE WEEK, FROM THE TOP.` · then, large: `WALK IT.`

segments.voice: Choose one of the eight for today, maybe right speech, right effort or right mindfulness, and let one picture come of what it would look like in the next few hours: a kinder sentence, one task done with full attention, a pause before reacting. Hold that picture for a few breaths. Then let it go, and just sit, the way a walker rests before setting off.
Bhāvetabba. To be developed, cultivated, brought into being: the fourth truth's task, the path walked again and again until it becomes a road.
Your line: walk it. One walk at a time, the grass gives way. That's the week.

howItsDone: Buddhists speak of bhāvanā, cultivation, for meditation and for the whole path; many choose a single factor, like right speech, to work on for a day or a retreat.
